composition.arrows: A slim curved ink route joins sheets; a cut triangular tip indicates direction without becoming another sheet.
composition.people: Separate cut-paper head, shoulders and torso overlap; a backing silhouette exposes the paper depth.
composition.empty: A cut chair from separate back, seat and legs, with visible vacancy; label the seat explicitly.
composition.pending: Place a cut clock disk and pointer alongside the waiting sheet; retain the pending label.
composition.emphasis: Overlap an accent cutout on a quiet sheet without obscuring the source/destination relationship.
composition.warning: Use a distinct labeled paper tab rather than an alarming shadow or extra data layer.

required.description: Build cut-paper silhouettes from overlapping planar pieces with visible cut edges and one offset shadow direction.
Preserve exact brief labels, locked relations and factual counts. Empty, pending and complete remain separate states. Inspect Japanese text at the actual placement.
Use the six semantic palette roles; every kit color-bearing element declares its role. Palette changes do not change geometry.
Use the scheme texture and fixed seed. Do not add random noise or distort text; no texture means no procedural texture.

preferred.description: Keep paper edges visible around labels; shadows and rotations must never imply extra factual objects.
Retain editorial spacing and optional serif sample lettering; required Japanese labels remain upright in the declared readable font.

flexible.description: Panel count, object placement, arrow routing and line breaks follow the actual brief and aspect ratio; the reference is not a page template.
Hand-author tone-native variations or omit nonessential detail. Explain departures from preferred rules and retain required facts.
Use the declared Japanese font for essential labels; decorative Latin lettering may reflect the original reference when it remains readable.
